claude.sample_unit: patient FAQs (10 oculoplastics conditions) plus 8 procedure explanations

links.outcome: Reading grade level of ChatGPT responses to patient FAQs versus Google
links.effect: ChatGPT responses averaged grade level 15.6 vs Google 10.0 (p<0.001); FRE 27.4 vs 48.5, far above the AMA-recommended 6th grade level.
links.quote: Responses to patient FAQs provided by ChatGPT were written at a significantly higher average grade level than responses provided by Google (15.6 vs 10.0, respectively, p < 0.001) ( Table 2 ).

links.outcome: Grade level of ChatGPT procedure explanations with and without a requested 7th grade reading level
links.effect: Requesting 7th grade level reduced average grade level from 15.7 to 11.7 (p<0.001), FRE 29.8 to 53.6, without sacrificing accuracy (3% inaccurate in both), but still above the requested level.
links.quote: When asking ChatGPT to generate patient education materials at a 7 th grade reading level, readability significantly improved to an average grade level of 11.7 (high school level) and a FRE of 53.6 (“fairly difficult”) (p < 0.001).

links.outcome: Expert-rated inaccurate or inappropriate content in ChatGPT versus Google FAQ responses
links.effect: Experts rated ChatGPT responses inaccurate/inappropriate 7% of the time versus Google 22% (p<0.001); ChatGPT procedure explanations flagged inaccurate in 3% of reviews.
links.quote: Responses provided by Google were rated to contain inaccurate or inappropriate information 22% of the time while responses provided by ChatGPT were rated to contain inaccurate or inappropriate information 7% of the time (p < 0.001).

links.outcome: FAQ accuracy and preference versus Google
links.effect: ChatGPT: 93% accuracy vs Google: 78% (p < 0.001); preferred by panelists 79%.
links.quote: ChatGPT responses (93% accuracy) were significantly more accurate (p < 0.001) than Google responses (78% accuracy) and were preferred by expert panelists (79%).

links.outcome: Achievement of requested patient-education reading level
links.effect: A 7th-grade request improved readability, but ChatGPT output was still written at a 12th-grade level.
links.quote: When instructed to provide responses at a 7 th grade reading level, the responses provided by ChatGPT were written at a 12 th grade level – an improvement compared to when no grade level was specified but still higher than the 7 th grade reading level requested.

links.effect: Unspecified and 7th-grade requested procedure texts were each labeled inaccurate on 3% of panelist reviews.
links.quote: Both the responses provided at the unspecified grade level and the responses generated after the 7 th grade reading level was requested were labeled as inaccurate on 3% of total panelist reviews.

links.effect: Google responses were inaccurate/inappropriate 22% of the time; ChatGPT responses 7% (p < 0.001).
links.quote: Responses provided by Google were rated to contain inaccurate or inappropriate information 22% of the time while responses provided by ChatGPT were rated to contain inaccurate or inappropriate information 7% of the time (p < 0.001).

links.outcome: Expert identification of AI-generated FAQ responses
links.effect: Among panelists making a choice, 31% (38/121) correctly identified the AI-generated response.
links.quote: Of the panelists who elected to make a selection, 31% (38/121) correctly identified the AI-generated response ( Table 5 ).

links.outcome: readability grade level of patient FAQ responses
links.effect: ChatGPT responses averaged grade level 15.6 vs Google 10.0 (p < 0.001); procedural explanations requested at 7th-grade level averaged grade 11.7 vs 15.7 unspecified (p < 0.001)
links.quote: ChatGPT responses to patient FAQs were written at a significantly higher average grade level than Google responses (grade 15.6 vs 10.0, p < 0.001).

unlisted_practices: Prompting generative AI to rewrite patient education materials at a specified target reading level

screen.reason: The study tests the ability of ChatGPT to accurately respond to patient questions and specifically evaluates a deployment practice/prompt safeguard (instructing the LLM to rewrite patient education materials at specified reading levels to adjust health literacy while preserving accuracy).
